mainTopic: Yoma 15b: The meaning of טהרו של מזבח, and why the order of blood placement for the תמיד, following רבי שמעון איש המצפה, is: עולה before חטאת, the northeast and southwest corners, and northeast first.
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier explanation: the word טהרו means the top surface of the altar itself, proven from the פסוק 'וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר'. The גמרא then returns to רבי שמעון איש המצפה's order of blood placement for the תמיד and asks three 'why this order?' questions. The עולה placement comes before the חטאת placement because the תמיד itself is an עולה. The northeast and southwest corners are used because an עולה needs a יסוד, and the southeast corner had none. The northeast comes first because every turn in the service goes to the right, so the כהן reaches it first. Next the גמרא asks how we know the עולה copies the חטאת's procedure and not the reverse; the word 'עַל' in 'עַל עוֹלַת הַתָּמִיד' shows that a feature of the חטאת is placed upon the עולה. Finally, a new topic begins: the משנה in תמיד puts the לשכת הטלאים in the northwest corner of the בית המוקד, but the משנה in מדות puts it in the southwest. The resolution of this contradiction comes on the next amud.

steps.title: טהרו means the top of the altar itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the word טהרו. It refers to the actual surface of the altar, based on the פסוק 'וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means on the body of the altar itself, as it is written: 'And like the very sky for purity.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an explanation that began before our passage. The גמרא says the word טהרו means the altar's own surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word טֹהַר in the פסוק describes a clear, pure brightness, like the sky. So טהרו של מזבח is the bare, shining gold top of the altar, once the ashes are cleared away. The proof is simply that the same Hebrew root is used for clear, exposed brightness.

keyTerms.meaning: The body (actual surface) of the altar
Its 'purity': here, the bare top surface of the altar
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: On the body of the altar itself,
phrases.notes: Answers the earlier question of what טהרו means.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And like the very sky for purity.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק is Exodus 24:10. Here טֹהַר means a clear brightness, like the gold top of the altar once it's uncovered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a definition of טהרו that the גמרא began on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טהרו is the surface of the altar itself, proven from 'וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר'.

steps.title: Why the burnt-offering procedure comes before the sin-offering procedure
steps.stepSummary: Going back to רבי שמעון איש המצפה, the גמרא asks why the עולה-style placement is done first and the חטאת-style placement second, instead of the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different that he places [blood the way of] the burnt-offering first, and then places [the way] of the sin-offering? Let him first place [the way] of the sin-offering, and then place [the way] of the burnt-offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי שמעון איש המצפה's order of service and asks why it goes in this particular order. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about order, not about whether these placements are required. A חטאת usually gets priority in the Temple, so one might expect it to come first. The גמרא wants to know why the עולה goes first here.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this way and not another?

phrases.english: What is different that he places [like] the burnt-offering first
phrases.notes: He's asking about the order רבי שמעון איש המצפה gave.

phrases.english: and then places [like] that of the sin-offering?
Let him first place [like] that of the sin-offering,
and then place [like] that of the burnt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the discussion of רבי שמעון איש המצפה after the side explanation of טהרו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the עולה procedure come before the חטאת procedure?

steps.title: The burnt-offering goes first because the תמיד is a burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: Since the תמיד itself is an עולה, the עולה procedure comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is a burnt-offering, it comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the offering being brought is an עולה, so its own procedure naturally comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main identity of the offering decides the order. The תמיד is an עולה, so the placement that matches its own category comes before the extra חטאת-style element.

phrases.english: Since it is a burnt-offering,
it comes first.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The offering is an עולה, so the עולה procedure takes precedence.

steps.title: Why the northeast and southwest corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the blood goes on the northeast and southwest corners, instead of the southeast and northwest corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different that he places [blood] on the northeast and the southwest? Let him place on the southeast, and then the northwest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second 'why this order' question, this time about which corners are used. It sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה gets שתי מתנות שהן ארבע: two diagonally opposite corners, so the blood touches all four sides. Either diagonal pair would do that equally well, so the גמרא asks why this pair was chosen.

phrases.english: And what is different that he places on the northeast [corner],
and the southwest [corner]?
Let him place on the southeast,
phrases.notes: That's the other pair of opposite corners.

phrases.english: and then the northwest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about the same order of service.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why use the NE/SW diagonal and not the SE/NW diagonal?

steps.title: A burnt-offering needs a corner with a base
steps.stepSummary: The blood of an עולה must go where there is a יסוד, and the southeast corner had no יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: a burnt-offering requires a base, and the southeast corner did not have a base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the עולה's blood must be placed above the יסוד, the base, which the southeast corner lacked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יסוד ran along the full north and west sides of the altar, but only one אמה into the south and east sides. So the southeast corner had no base at all. That rules out the SE/NW pair, which leaves the NE/SW pair.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the יסוד went all the way around the altar. It was missing from the southeast corner, and that is the whole reason for this answer.

phrases.english: They say: a burnt-offering requires a base,

phrases.aramaic: וְקֶרֶן דְּרוֹמִית מִזְרָחִית לָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ יְסוֹד.
phrases.english: and the southeast corner did not have a base.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עולה needs a יסוד under the blood, and the southeast corner has none.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the physical shape of the altar sets the halachic order of the blood placements.

steps.title: Why northeast before southwest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the northeast corner comes first, rather than starting at the southwest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different that he places first on the northeast and then the southwest? Let him place first on the southwest and then the northeast!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know which two corners are used, the גמרא asks why they go in this order. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both corners have a יסוד, so the reason from step 5 can't explain which one comes first. A new reason is needed.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּיָהֵיב בְּרֵישָׁא מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית
phrases.english: What is different that he places first on the northeast
and then the southwest?
Let him place first on the southwest
and then the northeast!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּיָהֵיב בְּרֵישָׁא מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 5: the corners are settled, so now the order between them is questioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the northeast corner done before the southwest?

steps.title: All turns go to the right, so the northeast is reached first
steps.stepSummary: Every turn in the Temple service must be to the right, toward the east. Following that path, the כהן reaches the northeast corner first, so he places the blood there first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said: all turns that you make should only be by way of the right, toward the east. He encounters that one first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using a general rule of Temple service: always turn right. That rule brings the כהן to the northeast corner first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is slaughtered on the north side. Moving from there and turning to the right, toward the east, the first corner the כהן reaches is the northeast. The rule is that you don't skip over a מצוה you meet first, so he places the blood where he arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting an established teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Three questions about order, three answers: (1) the עולה goes first because the תמיד is an עולה; (2) the corners are NE/SW because the southeast corner has no יסוד; (3) NE comes first because all turns are to the right, so the כהן reaches it first.

phrases.english: Since the Master said:
All turns that you turn

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין לַמִּזְרָח,
phrases.english: should be only by way of the right, toward the east,
[so] he encounters that one first.
phrases.notes: Coming from the north, where the animal is slaughtered, the northeast corner is reached first.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר כׇּל פִּינּוֹת שֶׁאַתָּה פּוֹנֶה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Turning right toward the east brings the כהן to the northeast corner first, so he places the blood there first.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of turning right appears throughout the Temple service and decides the order of many of its actions.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the opposite direction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier derivation. Perhaps the verse is telling us to do the חטאת like an עולה, rather than the עולה like a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the תורה is telling us to do the עולה the way we do a חטאת? Maybe it is telling us to do the חטאת the way we do an עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the direction of the earlier learning. Which קרבן is borrowing its procedure from which?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא used a verse to say that a feature of the חטאת procedure applies to the עולה. The challenge points out that the same verse links the two קרבנות, but it does not obviously say which one copies the other. If the copying went the other way, the earlier conclusion would collapse.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? / How do we know?
The Merciful One, i.e., the Torah

phrases.english: And from where [do we know] that it is regarding the burnt-offering
that the Merciful One says
perform with it the procedure of a sin-offering?
But perhaps it is regarding the sin-offering
that the Merciful One says
perform with it the procedure of a burnt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source behind the earlier claim that the עולה follows the חטאת procedure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the verse as applying the חטאת procedure to the עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse links the two offerings, but the direction of the transfer could just as well be reversed.

steps.title: The wording of the verse shows the direction
steps.stepSummary: The verse says the חטאת is offered "עַל עוֹלַת הַתָּמִיד", literally "upon" the עולה. So the חטאת's procedure is placed onto the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because the פסוק says "עַל עוֹלַת הַתָּמִיד יֵעָשֶׂה וְנִסְכּוֹ." What is the תורה saying? Take something from the חטאת and put it upon the עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the word "עַל" in the פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about the חטאת (the goat of ראש חודש) and says it is done "עַל" the עולת התמיד. The גמרא reads "עַל" as "upon": a feature of the חטאת is placed on top of the עולה. So the עולה receives the חטאת's procedure, and the earlier derivation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind, i.e., that idea is rejected
Its libation (wine poured with the offering)

steps.whatToRemember: The word "עַל" in the פסוק shows the direction: a rule of the חטאת is carried over onto the עולה, not the reverse.

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind,
as it is written:
"Upon (aside from) the daily burnt-offering
it shall be offered, and its libation"
What is the Merciful One saying?
Cast a matter of the sin-offering upon the burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by reading the פסוק closely.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the חטאת copies the עולה's procedure.
steps.terutzMaskana: "עַל עוֹלַת" means the חטאת's feature is placed upon the עולה, so the עולה follows the חטאת procedure.

steps.title: The משנה in תמיד: the Chamber of the Lambs is in the northwest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה. The ממונה sends the כהנים to bring a lamb from the לשכת הטלאים. That chamber is in the northwest corner of the בית המוקד, one of four chambers there.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: the ממונה said to them, "Go and bring a lamb from the Chamber of the Lambs." The Chamber of the Lambs was in the northwest corner. There were four chambers there: the Chamber of the Lambs, the Chamber of the Seals, the Chamber of the בית המוקד, and the chamber where they made the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a משנה from מסכת תמיד. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the location: this משנה places the לשכת הטלאים in the northwest corner. The גמרא is laying down this fact so it can compare it with another משנה. Like the earlier discussion, this contradiction will be resolved by showing that different תנאים hold different views.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, i.e., in a משנה in another tractate
The appointed official who directed the כהנים
The Chamber of the Lambs, where checked lambs were kept for קרבנות
The Chamber of the Seals, where receipt-tokens for buying offerings were kept
The Hall of the Hearth, a heated building in the Temple
The showbread placed on the שולחן

phrases.english: We learned there [in a mishna]:
The appointee said to them:
Go out and bring a lamb
from the Chamber of the Lambs.
And the Chamber of the Lambs
was in the northwest corner.
And there were four chambers there:
one, the Chamber of the Lambs,
and one, the Chamber of the Seals,
and one, the Chamber of the Hall of the Hearth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת לִשְׁכָּה שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בָּהּ לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
phrases.english: and one, the chamber in which they make the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: a second contradiction between sources, which will be resolved the same way as the earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה in תמיד, the לשכת הטלאים was in the northwest corner of the בית המוקד, one of four chambers there.

steps.title: The משנה in מדות puts the Chamber of the Lambs in the southwest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a contradicting משנה. It describes four chambers of the בית המוקד and says the chamber of the sacrificial lambs was in the southwest, not the northwest.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: There were four chambers belonging to the בית המוקד, like small rooms opening into a big hall. Two were in the holy area and two in the non-holy area. The tops of wooden stakes marked the line between holy and non-holy. What were they used for? The southwest one was the chamber of the lambs for קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places a different משנה against the first one. This one locates the lamb chamber in a different corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה said northwest, and this one says southwest. Both describe the four chambers of the same building, the בית המוקד, so the clash over the lamb chamber's corner is direct. This amud ends here. On the next amud, the גמרא continues the list and resolves the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction between them
Wooden stakes or markers marking a boundary

steps.confusionAlert: Both משניות describe four chambers of the same building, the בית המוקד. The clash in the text so far is the corner of the lamb chamber: northwest in the first משנה, southwest in this one. Do not assume the two lists of chambers are identical. The first משנה names the Chamber of the Seals and the Chamber of the בית המוקד, while this משנה, as it continues on the next amud, lists other chambers.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Four chambers belonged to the Hall of the Hearth,
like small rooms that open into a large hall,
two in the sacred area, and two in the non-sacred area,
and the tops of wooden stakes
divided between sacred and non-sacred.
And what purpose did they serve?
The southwest one —
it was the Chamber of the Sacrificial Lambs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: אַרְבַּע לְשָׁכוֹת הָיוּ לְבֵית הַמּוֹקֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the location given in the משנה of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה in תמיד placing the לשכת הטלאים in the northwest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in מדות places the same chamber in the southwest, so the two sources clash on its location.
